chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, who said: Muawiya ibn 'Ammar narrated to me, saying:

The sister of Mufaddal ibn Ghayath died, and she bequeathed from her wealth: one-third in the Way of Allah, one-third to the poor, and one-third for Hajj. However, the wealth did not reach the amount required to fulfill all three fully. So I and he went to Ibn Abi Layla and related the story to him. He said, 'Allocate one-third to this, one-third to that, and one-third to that.' Then we went to Ibn Shubrumah, and he also said what Ibn Abi Layla had said. Then we went to Abu Hanifah, and he said as they both had said.

So we went to Mecca, and he said to me, 'Ask Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).' The woman had not yet performed Hajj. So I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and he said to me, 'Begin with Hajj, for it is an obligation from Allah upon her. And whatever remains, allocate part of it to this and part of it to that.'

He (the narrator) said: So I proceeded and entered the mosque, and I faced Abu Hanifah and said to him, 'I asked Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) about that which I asked you about, and he said to me,
By Allah, he neither said good to me nor bad. And I came to his circle (gathering), and they had spread it out (as a ruling), and they said, 'Abu Hanifah said,
I said, 'By Allah, it was such and such (anyway).' So they said, 'He (Abu Hanifah) informed us of this.'
I said, 'By Allah, it was such and such.' So they said, 'He informed us of this.'

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: How should a deceased person's bequest be distributed if the wealth is insufficient to fulfill all bequests, particularly when one involves Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith highlights the jurisprudential principle of prioritizing missed divine obligations (Hajj) over voluntary bequests, contrasting the equal-split approach of early jurists like Abu Hanifah with Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq’s (AS) ruling. It underscores the Shia emphasis on distinguishing between Fard (obligatory) and Nafl (voluntary) acts when allocating limited estate resources. The narrative also serves as a validation of the Imam’s authority, as the narrator confirms the accuracy of the report despite the jurists' differing opinions.
